# core


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

This module builds the index that shows whether your code or one of your
dependencies already has a helper you need. It splits source files into
chunks, one per function, class or method. It stores each chunk with its
metadata and an embedding. An embedding is a vector of numbers computed
from the code, and chunks with similar meaning have similar vectors. A
search combines two methods. Keyword search (SQLite’s FTS5) finds chunks
that contain the words of the query. Vector search finds chunks whose
embedding is close to the query’s embedding. No language model is
involved, and everything runs locally.

There are two indexes. The repo index covers your own code and lives in
`.kosha/code.db` inside the repository. The package index covers
installed packages and lives in your user data directory
(`~/.local/share/kosha/env.db` on most systems). Every project on the
machine shares it, and a package version is indexed once. The `Kosha`
class owns both indexes. The `graph` module holds the call graph built
from them.

## Utilities

These helpers support the indexing code below. Most users never call
them directly.

`parse` reads Python source, from a string or a file path, and returns
its syntax tree along with what kosha needs from it: a map from each
imported name to its top-level package, the names of top-level functions
and classes, the same plus module-level names assigned from a call, and
a map from each imported name to its full dotted path. Results are
cached, so calling it again on the same input is free. Source that does
not parse gives `None` and empty collections.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### parse

``` python
def parse(
    code:NoneType=None, p:NoneType=None
):
```

*Parse `code` or the file `p` and return (tree, imports, top-level defs,
defs plus call-assigned names, import paths).*

The package includes a `SKILL.md` file that tells coding agents how to
use kosha. `mv_skill_md` copies it to `.agents/skills/kosha/SKILL.md`
and `.claude/skills/kosha/SKILL.md` in the repository, or under `dir` if
you give one. By default it prints the target paths and copies nothing.
Pass `dry_run=False` to write the files. `Kosha(install_skill=True)` and
the `kosha install` command call it for you.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

``` python
)->None:
```

*Copy the bundled SKILL.md into `.agents/skills/kosha/` and
`.claude/skills/kosha/`; `dry_run` only prints the targets.*

`arun` runs a coroutine from ordinary code. `asyncio.run` fails inside a
running event loop, and Jupyter notebook code runs inside one. In that
case `arun` runs the coroutine in a worker thread with its own loop.
`arun` returns the result wrapped in a fastcore `L`. The two tests below
show both paths.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### arun

``` python
def arun(
    coro
)-><built-in function any>:
```

*Run `coro` to completion from synchronous code, even inside a running
event loop, and return its result in an `L`.*

``` python
async def _add(a, b): return a + b
assert arun(_add(1, 2)) == L(3)
print('arun: sync context ok')
```

    arun: sync context ok

``` python
async def _test_nested():
    result = arun(_add(10, 20))
    assert first(result) == 30, f'got {result}'
arun(_test_nested())
print('arun: nested-loop context ok')
```

    arun: nested-loop context ok

To decide which packages to index, kosha starts from the dependencies
listed in your `pyproject.toml` and follows their own requirements.
`pkg_trans_deps(seeds, depth)` does the walk. It returns the seed
packages plus the packages they require, `depth` levels down. It keeps
only installed packages and skips optional extras. With `depth=0` it
returns the seeds.

`env_pkg_versions` returns {package name: installed version} for the
packages to index. With `pyproject=True`, the default, it starts from
the dependencies in `pyproject.toml` and expands `depth` levels with
`pkg_trans_deps`. It returns an empty dict when there is no repository
root or no `pyproject.toml`. With `pyproject=False` it returns every
installed package. The examples show both.

## Kosha

`Kosha` is the object you work with. Create one in your repository with
`Kosha()`. It finds the repository root, opens the repo index in
`.kosha/code.db` and the shared package index in the user data
directory, and loads the embedding model. Its arguments let you point it
somewhere else: `dir` sets the repository root, `xdg_dir` the data
directory that holds the package index, and `efn` the embedding model,
by default litesearch’s static code embedder. `install_skill=True` also
installs `SKILL.md`. Set `busy_timeout` (in milliseconds) when several
processes or threads write to the index at once, as
`update_pkgs(parallel=True)` does.

Inside, the object holds three stores: `code_st` for repo chunks,
`env_st` for package chunks, and `pkg_st` for package descriptions. Four
plain tables sit beside them. `packages` records each indexed package
version, and `pkg_deps` and `repo_deps` count which packages each
package or repo module imports. `repo_file_imports` keeps the packages
each repo file imports, so an incremental `update_repo` recounts
`repo_deps` without parsing unchanged files.

`cast_emb` makes sure every vector kosha stores has the data type the
search code reads back (16-bit floats), whatever the embedding model
returns.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

`pkg_url` returns the best web address for an installed package from its
metadata: the source code link if there is one, then the repository,
then the home page, then any project URL. Hand it to a web search or
fetch tool when you need a package’s changelog or documentation.
`pkg_doc` builds a description record of a package. The content is its
summary and the first 2,000 characters of its README. The metadata holds
name, version, keywords, requirements, summary and URL.

Chunk names are dotted paths like
[`fastcore.basics.merge`](https://fastcore.fast.ai/basics.html#merge).
To build them, kosha needs a file’s import root: the directory a Python
import starts from. `has_init` checks whether a directory is a package
(it holds an `__init__.py` or a compiled `__init__` module), and
`imp_root` climbs from a file to the nearest ancestor that is not a
package.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

``` python
def imp_root(
    p:pathlib.Path
)->pathlib.Path:
```

*The directory imports of `p` start from: its nearest ancestor that is
not a package.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

``` python
def has_init(
    d:pathlib.Path
)->bool:
```

*True if `d` is a Python package directory: it holds `__init__.py` or a
compiled `__init__*.so`.*

litesearch’s `file_parse` splits a file into chunks, one per top-level
function, class or assignment. `enrich_chunks` prepares them for the
index. It marks each chunk as public API or not. A name is public when
it is in the module’s `__all__`, or, when the module has no `__all__`,
when it has no leading underscore. It records the docstring. It adds
every method of a class as a chunk of its own, so a search can return
`Table.insert_all` and not only `Table`. `enrich_chunks` reads
assignment chunks only to find `__all__` and does not return them.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### enrich_chunks

``` python
def enrich_chunks(
    content:fastcore.foundation.L
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
```

*Mark chunks as public or private, record their docstrings, add one
chunk per class method, and drop assignment chunks.*

## Indexing packages

`update_pkg` indexes one installed package. It parses the package’s
source files into chunks, stores them in the package index with an
embedding, and records in `pkg_deps` how many of its modules import each
other package. A package already indexed at its installed version is not
parsed again, unless you pass `force=True`, but any of its chunks still
without an embedding are embedded. `update_pkgs` does the same for a
list. Use `parallel=True` to index several packages in threads at once;
that needs a `Kosha` built with a `busy_timeout`, and without one it
raises an error, as the test below shows. `rm_pkg` removes a package, or
one version of it, from the index.

`process_env` computes embeddings for package chunks that were stored
without one, for example after `update_pkgs(embed=False)`;
`reembed=True` recomputes all of them. It works through `embed_missing`,
which does the same for any store and keeps its HNSW index in step.
`nuke` deletes the repo’s `.kosha` directory, which holds the repo index
and the call graph, and with `env=True` also the shared data directory
holding the package and docs indexes. `count_imp` counts, for a list of
files, how many import each top-level package.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Kosha.update_pkgs

``` python
def update_pkgs(
    pkgs:str | list=None, # package name or list of names to index; nothing happens if empty
    embed:bool=True, # embed chunks after indexing
    exts:str='.py,.js,.ts,.jsx,.tsx,.java,.go,.cs,.ruby,.php,.swift,.kt,.kts,.rs,.scala,.lua', # file extensions to include
    verbose:bool=True, # print progress
    force:bool=False, # reindex even if package version already loaded

    **kwargs
):
```

``` python
# update_pkgs(parallel=True) refuses without a busy timeout. Concurrent database() opens would hit
# apsw's 100ms default and raise SQLITE_BUSY inside the open hook. That drops whole packages and no
# exception reaches the caller. A silently incomplete index is worse than a loud failure.
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
_gt = tempfile.mkdtemp(); _gk = Kosha(dir=_gt, xdg_dir=Path(_gt))
assert _gk.busy_timeout is None
try:
    _gk.update_pkgs(['certifi'], parallel=True, embed=False, verbose=False)
    assert False, 'parallel=True without busy_timeout must raise'
except ValueError as e: assert 'busy timeout' in str(e)
_gk.update_pkgs(['certifi'], parallel=False, embed=False, verbose=False)   # serial path is unguarded
assert len(_gk.env_st()) > 0

# with a timeout set, threaded ingestion must store exactly what the serial path stores
_pk = ['certifi', 'idna', 'fastlite']
_ta, _tb = tempfile.mkdtemp(), tempfile.mkdtemp()
_ka = Kosha(dir=_ta, xdg_dir=Path(_ta), busy_timeout=30_000)
_kb = Kosha(dir=_tb, xdg_dir=Path(_tb), busy_timeout=30_000)
_ka.update_pkgs(_pk, parallel=True,  embed=False, verbose=False)
_kb.update_pkgs(_pk, parallel=False, embed=False, verbose=False)
assert {r['name'] for r in _ka.pkgs(select='name')} == set(_pk), 'parallel lost a package'
assert len(_ka.env_st()) == len(_kb.env_st()), 'parallel dropped rows vs serial'
```

`Kosha` finds the project’s own environment once, in `Kosha.env_path`:
the `.venv` in its root, else `$VIRTUAL_ENV` when that lies inside the
root. kosha reads packages from that environment and not from the
interpreter that runs kosha. A package installed only in the project’s
`.venv` appears in `status` and `update_pkg` indexes it, with the
version and file paths of that copy. When there is no such environment,
`env_path` is empty and kosha uses the running interpreter.

``` python
from fastcore.test import test_eq
```

`sync(embed=False)` stores chunks for keyword search only. Indexing the
same package again with embeddings on embeds those chunks too, even
though the package is already loaded at its installed version. A first
sync with `embed=False` does not leave the package invisible to vector
search.

``` python
_et = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()); _er, _esp = _fake_proj(_et, 'proj')
_fake_dist(_esp, 'kkledger', '1.0', 'def parse_ledger(path): return open(path).read().split()\n\ndef sum_ledger(rows): return sum(map(float, rows))\n')
_ek = Kosha(dir=_er, xdg_dir=_et/'xdg')
_ek.update_pkg('kkledger', embed=False, verbose=False)
_nulls = lambda: (len(_ek.env_st(where="package='kkledger' AND embedding IS NULL")), len(_ek.pkg_st(where='embedding IS NULL')))
_unembedded = _nulls()
_ek.update_pkg('kkledger', verbose=False)
test_eq((_unembedded, _nulls()), ((2, 1), (0, 0)))
_unembedded, _nulls()
```

Chunks stored without an embedding before that behaviour existed need a
backfill. `process_env` embeds every such chunk, `batch` at a time. It
commits each batch and adds it to the HNSW index in the same step. An
interrupted backfill resumes where it stopped. Vector search sees each
chunk as soon as the chunk has a vector:

``` python
_fake_dist(_esp, 'kkinvoice', '2.0', 'def render_invoice(order): return f"Invoice {order}"\n\ndef email_invoice(addr, pdf): pass\n\ndef void_invoice(n): return -n\n')
_ek.update_pkg('kkinvoice', embed=False, verbose=False)
_idx = lambda: _ek.envdb.get_index(_ek.env_st.name)
_size = _idx().size
_done = _ek.process_env(batch=2)
test_eq((_done, _idx().size - _size, len(_ek.env_st(where='embedding IS NULL'))), (3, 3, 0))
_nearest(_ek, 'render an invoice for an order')
```

## Indexing the repository

`update_repo` indexes your own code. It walks the repository, skipping
folders whose names start with `.` or `_` and the `build` and `dist`
folders, and skipping files whose names start with `.` or `_` as well as
`setup.py` and `conftest.py`. It compares each file’s modification time
with the time recorded at the last run. It re-parses only files that are
new or changed, and deletes chunks of files that are gone. It also
records in `repo_deps` how many repo files import each installed
package. `force=True` re-indexes every file. `files=` limits the run to
the listed paths, as `watch_repo` does for each change event.
`update_repo` deletes the chunks of a listed path that no longer exists.
`process_repo` embeds repo chunks that were stored without an embedding.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Kosha.update_repo

``` python
def update_repo(
    dir:pathlib.Path=None, # directory to index; defaults to repo root
    embed:bool=True, # embed chunks after parsing
    exts:str='.py,.js,.ts,.jsx,.tsx,.java,.go,.cs,.ruby,.php,.swift,.kt,.kts,.rs,.scala,.lua', # file extensions to index
    verbose:bool=True, # print progress
    force:bool=False, # re-index every file, changed or not
    files:list=None, # only these paths, as from a watch event; listed paths that are gone are dropped
    *, skip_file_re:str='^[.]|^(?:setup\\.py|conftest\\.py)$',
    skip_folder_re:str='^[.]|^(?:tests?|examples?|docs?|build|dist|_proc|_docs|_site|_site_libs|node_modules|__pycache__)$',
    func:type=Path, path:pathlib.Path | str='.', recursive:bool=True, maxdepth:int=None, symlinks:bool=True,
    file_glob:str=None, file_re:str=None, path_glob:str=None, path_re:str=None, folder_re:str=None,
    skip_file_glob:str=None, ret_folders:bool=False, sort:bool=True, types:str | list=None
):
```

*Index new and changed repo files under `dir` and drop the chunks of
deleted ones.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Kosha.process_repo

``` python
def process_repo(
    content:NoneType=None, reembed:bool=False, *, embed:bool=True, emb_fn:NoneType=None,
    hash_id_columns:tuple=('content',), parallel:bool=False, chunk:int=1000
):
```

*Embed repo chunks that have no embedding yet, or all of them with
`reembed=True`.*

``` python
# update_repo(files=...) as watch_repo calls it: only listed paths are touched, and a listed path that is gone is dropped.
_wt = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()); _wk = Kosha(dir=_wt, xdg_dir=_wt)
for _n in 'abc': (_wt/f'{_n}.py').write_text(f'def {_n}(): pass\n')
_wk.update_repo(embed=False, verbose=False)
(_wt/'a.py').write_text('def a2(): pass\n'); (_wt/'b.py').unlink(); (_wt/'c.py').write_text('def c2(): pass\n')
_wk.update_repo(files=[_wt/'a.py', _wt/'b.py'], embed=False, verbose=False)
assert set(L(_wk.code_st(select='metadata')).map(lambda r: jl(r['metadata'])['name'])) == {'a2','c'}
(_wt/'sub').mkdir(); (_wt/'sub'/'d.py').write_text('def d(): pass\n')
_wk.update_repo(dir=_wt/'sub', embed=False, verbose=False)
assert {'a2','c','d'} <= set(L(_wk.code_st(select='metadata')).map(lambda r: jl(r['metadata'])['name'])), 'indexing a subdirectory keeps records outside it'
```

A file that fails to parse, such as an empty notebook, is skipped and
the rest are indexed. An edit above a function moves it without changing
its text. `update_repo` records the new `lineno`. A lookup by name reads
the `json_extract(metadata,'$.name')` index and does not scan the store.
`update_repo` drops the chunks of a deleted file only when the file lies
under `dir`. An index written before `CODE_FORMAT` 2 can hold old line
numbers and lacks the stored imports of each file. When `Kosha` opens
such an index, it marks every indexed file for re-parsing and sets the
format to 2. The next `update_repo` re-parses those files.

``` python
_mt = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()); _mk = Kosha(dir=_mt, xdg_dir=_mt)
(_mt/'m.py').write_text('def f(): pass\n\ndef g(): pass\n'); (_mt/'empty.ipynb').write_text('')
_mk.update_repo(embed=False, verbose=False, exts=code_exts+',.ipynb')
assert _mk.code_st(select='count(*) n')[0]['n'] == 2, 'an empty notebook beside it stops nothing'
(_mt/'m.py').write_text('X = 1\ndef f(): pass\n\ndef g2(): pass\n')
_mk.update_repo(embed=False, verbose=False)
_lines = lambda k: {jl(r['metadata'])['name']: jl(r['metadata'])['lineno'] for r in k.code_st(select='metadata')}
assert _lines(_mk)['f'] == 2, _lines(_mk)
_plan = _mk.codedb.q(f"explain query plan select id from [{_mk.code_st.name}] where json_extract(metadata, '$.name') = ?", ['f'])
assert any('_name' in r['detail'] for r in _plan), _plan
_mk.codedb.execute(f"update [{_mk.code_st.name}] set metadata=json_set(metadata,'$.lineno',99)")
_mk.codedb.execute('pragma user_version=0')
_mk2 = Kosha(dir=_mt, xdg_dir=_mt); _mk2.update_repo(embed=False, verbose=False)
assert _lines(_mk2)['f'] == 2, _lines(_mk2)
_fixed = _lines(_mk2)
(_mt/'m.py').write_text('from os import path\n__all__ = ["path"]\n'); _mk2.update_repo(embed=False, verbose=False)
assert _lines(_mk2) == {}, 'a file whose definitions all moved away keeps none of them'
_deps = lambda: {r['to_pkg']: r['n_files'] for r in _mk2.code_rd()}
(_mt/'a.py').write_text('import json\n'); (_mt/'b.py').write_text('import json\n'); _mk2.update_repo(embed=False, verbose=False)
assert _deps()['json'] == 2
(_mt/'a.py').write_text('import json\nx = 1\n'); os.utime(_mt/'a.py', (2e9, 2e9)); _mk2.update_repo(embed=False, verbose=False)
assert _deps()['json'] == 2, 'editing one importer keeps the other in the count'
for _n in 'ab': (_mt/f'{_n}.py').write_text('x = 1\n'); os.utime(_mt/f'{_n}.py', (2e9+1, 2e9+1))
_mk2.update_repo(embed=False, verbose=False)
assert 'json' not in _deps(), 'a package no file imports any more is dropped'
_fixed
```

When you upgrade a package, the index can hold rows for both versions.
`prune_old_versions` keeps only the highest version of one package. It
applies to the package’s chunks, its description and its `packages` row.
`prune_old_pkgs` does the same for every package. `pkgs_in_env` returns
the indexed packages whose version matches the installed one.

The cells after this one are checks and examples: module names built
from the import root, the file lists the repo walk produces with and
without the strict skip rules, and direct queries on the stores. Cells
marked `eval: false` index real packages. The docs build does not run
them.

------------------------------------------------------------------------


*Keep only the highest indexed version of `pkg`.*

``` python
# prune_old_versions drops chunks by their `package` column; metadata.name is the chunk's symbol name.
_vt = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()); _vk = Kosha(dir=_vt, xdg_dir=_vt)
_vk.update_pkg('certifi', embed=False, verbose=False)
process_content(_vk.env_st, [dict(content='def old(): pass', package='certifi', metadata=dict(name='old', version='0.0.1'))], embed=False)
_vk.pkgs.insert(dict(name='certifi', version='0.0.1'))
_n = len(_vk.env_st(where="package='certifi'"))
_vk.prune_old_versions('certifi')
assert len(_vk.env_st(where="package='certifi'")) == _n-1
assert [r['version'] for r in _vk.pkgs(where="name='certifi'")] == [_dist('certifi').version]
```

Every project on the machine shares the package index. The index can
therefore hold packages that no environment has any more, such as a
dependency you removed or every package of a project folder you deleted.
`prune_env` removes them. It judges what is installed by the
`*.dist-info` folders in each site-packages folder it knows. It lists
folders and never imports a package. It knows these folders: the folders
the indexed chunks were read from, the nearest `.venv` above an editable
install’s source, and the current project’s environment. A folder that
no longer exists holds nothing.

A package keeps its chunks while any of those folders holds it at any
version. A package has one set of chunks in the index, from whichever
version was synced last. A chunk’s `version` records the version at
which the chunk was first stored. An unchanged function from an old
release is still current code. A chunk’s `version` does not identify
stale chunks. Each `packages` row, one per indexed version, stays while
some folder holds that exact version. Removing a package also drops its
description and import counts. `prune_env` then runs `VACUUM` once to
shrink the file. After that it rebuilds the chunk index and the
package-description index once each. Each of these two indexes is an
approximate nearest-neighbour index of the HNSW kind.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Kosha.prune_env

``` python
def prune_env(
    dry_run:bool=False
)->dict:
```

*Remove the packages no known site-packages folder holds and the
versions none holds, compact env.db, and return what was removed.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### installed_dists

``` python
def installed_dists(
    root

```

*{normalized name: {version: metadata folder}} of the distributions
installed in site-packages folder `root`; empty when it is gone.*

Two projects share one index here. The first has `kktax` 1.0 and `kkfx`
1.0 installed, the second has `kktax` 2.0, so the index holds three
package versions:

``` python
_pt = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()); _pa, _spa = _fake_proj(_pt, 'old'); _pb, _spb = _fake_proj(_pt, 'new')
_fake_dist(_spa, 'kktax', '1.0', 'def vat(x): return x*0.2\n')
_fake_dist(_spb, 'kktax', '2.0', 'def vat(x, rate=0.2): return x*rate\n')
_fxdi = _fake_dist(_spa, 'kkfx', '1.0', 'def convert_currency(amount, rate): return amount*rate\n')
_kold, _knew = Kosha(dir=_pa, xdg_dir=_pt/'xdg'), Kosha(dir=_pb, xdg_dir=_pt/'xdg')
for _p in ('kktax', 'kkfx'): _kold.update_pkg(_p, verbose=False)
_knew.update_pkg('kktax', verbose=False)
_vers = lambda: sorted((r['name'], r['version']) for r in _kold.pkgs(select='name, version'))
_vers()
```

Uninstalling `kkfx` from the first project deletes its dist-info folder.
A dry run then lists `kkfx` 1.0 as stale and removes nothing. `kktax`
1.0 is not listed. The second project has a newer `kktax`, and the first
project’s site-packages still holds 1.0.

``` python
_fxdi.delete()
_dry = _kold.prune_env(dry_run=True)
test_eq(_pruned(_dry), (['kkfx'], [('kkfx', '1.0')]))
test_eq(len(_vers()), 3)
_dry
```

The real run removes `kkfx` and its chunks, keeps both `kktax` versions,
and leaves the HNSW index holding exactly the vectors still in the
table. Vector search keeps working:

``` python
test_eq(_pruned(_kold.prune_env()), _pruned(_dry))
_n_vec = lambda: (_kold.envdb.get_index(_kold.env_st.name).size, len(_kold.env_st(where='embedding IS NOT NULL')))
test_eq((_vers(), len(_kold.env_st(where="package='kkfx'"))), ([('kktax', '1.0'), ('kktax', '2.0')], 0))
test_eq(*_n_vec())
_nearest(_kold, 'value added tax rate')
```

Deleting the second project removes its site-packages folder, the only
place `kktax` 2.0 was installed. The 2.0 record goes. `kktax` keeps its
chunks because the first project still has it:

``` python
_pb.delete()
test_eq(_pruned(_kold.prune_env()), ([], [('kktax', '2.0')]))
test_eq(*_n_vec())
_vers(), len(_kold.env_st(where="package='kktax'"))
```

## Searching

A query can carry filters as `key:value` tokens next to the words, as in
`merge dicts package:fastcore path:basics`. `parseq` splits a query into
the plain text and a dict of filters. The keys are `file`, `path`,
`package`, `lang` and `type`, and the short forms people tend to type
first also work: `pkg`, `dir`, `folder`, `ext`, plurals such as
`packages`, and so on. A value can list several options separated by
commas. A trailing `!`, as in `package!:fastcore`, is accepted and means
the same as without it, because every filter already excludes everything
that does not match. A token that looks like a filter but has an unknown
key, such as `libr:litesearch`, is reported under `_unknown`, so a
caller can warn about it instead of silently searching for the literal
text. If a query holds nothing but filters, the whole query is kept as
the search text.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### parseq

``` python
def parseq(
    q:str
)->tuple:
```

*Split query `q` into its plain text and a dict of `key:value` filters,
with unknown keys under `_unknown`.*

``` python
# aliases and the `!` suffix resolve to the canonical key
for tok in ['package:litesearch', 'pkg:litesearch', 'pkgs:litesearch', 'package!:litesearch', 'pkg!:litesearch']:
    raw, fs = parseq(f'how do I add indexes with {tok}')
    assert fs['package'] == ['litesearch'], (tok, dict(fs))
    assert raw == 'how do I add indexes with', (tok, raw)
assert parseq('atomic save dir:xtras')[1]['path'] == ['xtras']
assert parseq('atomic save ext:py')[1]['lang'] == ['py']
assert parseq('search package:httpx,requests')[1]['package'] == ['httpx', 'requests']

# an unknown filter key is reported, not silently searched as text
assert parseq('add indexes with libr:litesearch')[1]['_unknown'] == ['libr']
assert parseq('add indexes with module:foo')[1]['_unknown'] == ['module']
# ...and known keys, urls and bare prose never trip it
for q in ['add indexes with package:litesearch', 'see https://example.com/x', 'how do I add indexes']:
    assert '_unknown' not in parseq(q)[1], q
```

``` python
parseq('how do I merge dicts package:fastcore path:data*')
```

    ('how do I merge dicts',
     defaultdict(list, {'package': ['fastcore'], 'path': ['data*']}))

``` python
assert parseq('stripe payments package:fasthtml file:routes*') == ('stripe payments', {'package': ['fasthtml'], 'file': ['routes*']})
assert parseq('package:monsterui package:fasthtml create a table') == ('create a table', {'package': ['monsterui', 'fasthtml']})
assert parseq('no filters here') == ('no filters here', {})
assert parseq('type:FunctionDef lang:py') == ('type:FunctionDef lang:py', {'type': ['FunctionDef'], 'lang': ['py']})
assert parseq('package:only')[0] == 'package:only'
# plural forms + comma-separated values
assert parseq('merge dicts packages:fastcore,litesearch') == ('merge dicts', {'package': ['fastcore', 'litesearch']})
assert parseq('search paths:basics,core,data') == ('search', {'path': ['basics', 'core', 'data']})
assert parseq('query packages:fastcore,litesearch paths:basics,core') == ('query', {'package': ['fastcore', 'litesearch'], 'path': ['basics', 'core']})
assert parseq('langs:py,js files:routes*,api*') == ('langs:py,js files:routes*,api*', {'lang': ['py', 'js'], 'file': ['routes*', 'api*']})
print('parse_query: all assertions pass')
```

`filt2wh` turns those filters into an SQL `WHERE` clause for one of the
two indexes. `file` and `path` values are globs (`*` and `?`) matched
anywhere in the path. `lang` takes an extension or a language name (`py`
or `python`). `type` matches the chunk’s syntax type, such as
`FunctionDef` or `ClassDef`. `package` applies only to the package
index, so on the repo index a filter dict holding only a package gives
`None`, meaning no filter.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### filt2wh

``` python
def filt2wh(
    filters:dict, store:str='code'
)->str | None:
```

*An SQL WHERE clause for `filters` (from `parseq`) on the `code` or
`env` store, or None if nothing applies.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### sql_str

``` python
def sql_str(
    v
)->str:
```

*`v` as an SQLite string literal: single-quoted, with each internal
quote doubled.*

``` python
# a `lang:` filter is answered from idx_store_lang on both stores, not by reading every row's metadata JSON
for _db, _s in ((k.codedb, 'code'), (k.envdb, 'env')):
    _plan = ' '.join(r['detail'] for r in _db.q(f"explain query plan select rowid from store where {filt2wh(parseq('x lang:rs')[1], _s)}"))
    assert 'idx_store_lang' in _plan, _plan
```

``` python
filt2wh(parseq('how do I merge dicts package:fastcore path:data*')[1], 'env')
```

    "(json_extract(metadata, '$.path') like '%data%') AND (package='fastcore')"

``` python
filt2wh({'type': ['FunctionDef']}, 'code')
```

    "(json_extract(metadata, '$.type') = 'FunctionDef')"

``` python
assert filt2wh({'file': ['routes*']}, 'code') == "(path LIKE '%routes%')"
assert filt2wh({'path': ['api/*']}, 'code') == "(path LIKE '%api/%')"
assert filt2wh({'lang': ['py']}, 'code') == "(json_extract(metadata, '$.lang') = '.py')"
assert filt2wh({'lang': ['python']}, 'code') == "(json_extract(metadata, '$.lang') = '.py')"
assert filt2wh({'package': ['fasthtml']}, 'env') == "(package='fasthtml')"
assert filt2wh({'type': ['FunctionDef']}, 'code') == "(json_extract(metadata, '$.type') = 'FunctionDef')"
assert filt2wh({}, 'code') is None
assert filt2wh({}, 'env') is None
assert filt2wh({'package': ['fasthtml']}, 'code') is None
print('filters_to_where: all assertions pass')
```

    filters_to_where: all assertions pass

`filt2wh` quotes every filter value with `sql_str`. A value is always
one SQL string literal, whatever quotes it holds. A value that holds a
quote of either kind matches that literal text and never changes the
clause. `sql_str` raises `ValueError` for a value that holds a NUL
character. Ordinary values give the same text as before.

``` python
import sqlite3
from fastcore.test import expect_fail
```

``` python
_qdb = sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
_qdb.execute('create table store(package text, metadata text, path text)')
_qdb.executemany('insert into store values (?, ?, ?)', [('x', '{}', 'a.py'), ('y', '{}', 'b.py')])
_qrows = lambda fs: [r[0] for r in _qdb.execute(f"select package from store where {filt2wh(fs, 'env')}")]
_qodd = ['x"\' OR 1=1 --', "it's", parseq('q package:x"\' OR 1=1 --')[1]['package'][0]]
test_eq([_qrows({'package': [v]}) for v in _qodd], [[], [], []])
test_eq(_qrows({'package': ['x']}), ['x'])
test_eq(filt2wh({'package': ['x', 'y']}, 'env'), "(package='x' OR package='y')")
with expect_fail(ValueError, contains='NUL'): sql_str('a\x00b')
filt2wh({'package': [_qodd[0]]}, 'env')
```

`env_context` searches the package index and `repo_context` searches the
repo index. Each parses the filters, embeds the query, runs one search
that combines keyword and vector matching, and returns hits with their
content and metadata. Use one of them when you know which index you
want. `Kosha.context`, defined in the `graph` module, searches both
indexes, reranks the hits for code and adds call-graph details. Use
`Kosha.context` by default.

Both take `limit`, an extra SQL `where`, and `rerank=True` to reorder
the hits with a flashrank cross-encoder, a small model that scores each
hit against the query. When reranking, kosha first retrieves a wider
pool of candidates (`fanout`) for the reranker to choose from. It then
cuts the result to `limit`. `pkgs2consider` returns the names of indexed
packages, or with `sys_wide=False` only those indexed at the version
your project uses.

``` python
# `wide` was accepted and ignored; the FTS leg always ORs the query terms through litesearch's `pre`.
```

`watch_repo` keeps the repo index current while you work. It blocks and
watches the repository with watchfiles. After every change it calls
`update_repo` with the changed files. It runs until you press Ctrl-C.
`awatch_repo` is the same loop as a coroutine, for code that already
runs an event loop.

## One row shape

A tool that shows kosha hits next to hits from other sources, such as
documentation or notes, needs every hit in one format. `code_row` turns
one hit from `repo_context` or `env_context` into an `AttrDict` with six
keys: `source` (which index the hit came from), `ref` (the dotted name,
or the path), `title`, `where` (`path:line`), `text` (the first 600
characters of the chunk) and `open`. `open` is a hint for how to open
the hit, such as `symbol('pkg.mod')`. `rows` runs the searches and
returns the hits in that format. It searches the repo index by default.
Pass `env=True` to add the package index.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

``` python
    q:str, # query, with kosha's key:value filters
    limit:int=12, repo:bool=True, # the repo index
    env:bool=False, # the installed-package index
    **kw
)->fastcore.foundation.L: # forwarded to repo_context / env_context
```

*Search hits for `q` from the repo and, with `env=True`, the package
index, each as a `code_row`.*


`pkg_context` searches package descriptions, the records `pkg_doc`
builds, to find a package by what it does. It reads the `pkg_store`
table, which `update_pkg` fills with one record per package through
`put_pkg_doc`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

*Keyword and vector search over the package descriptions in pkg_store.*

``` python
# update_pkg fills pkg_store with one description per package; reindexing replaces it rather than adding another.
_pt = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()); _pkk = Kosha(dir=_pt, xdg_dir=_pt)
_pkk.update_pkg('certifi', verbose=False); _pkk.update_pkg('certifi', verbose=False, force=True)
assert len(_pkk.pkg_st()) == 1
_r = _pkk.pkg_context('Mozilla CA bundle certificates', limit=3)
assert _r and _r[0]['metadata']['name'] == 'certifi', _r
```

``` python
# `cast_emb` pins the stored dtype to what `Database.search` reads back (float16), so a
# custom `efn` emitting float32 can no longer corrupt the vector leg silently.
emb = k.emb_doc(['def f(): pass'])
qry = k.emb_query('a function')
assert emb.dtype == DTYPE == np.float16, emb.dtype
assert qry.dtype == DTYPE, qry.dtype

f32 = cast_emb(lambda txts, **kw: np.zeros((len(txts), 4), dtype=np.float32))
assert f32(['a','b']).dtype == DTYPE
```

``` python
# rerank fans out to RERANK_FANOUT candidates, then the cross-encoder cuts back to `limit`.
assert fanout({}, 5, True)['limit'] == RERANK_FANOUT
assert fanout({}, 50, True)['limit'] == 50
assert fanout({}, 5, False)['limit'] == 5

# the live leg needs flashrank's model on disk; skip rather than fail on a cold/offline machine.
try: rr = k.env_context('atomic file write', limit=5, rerank=True)
except Exception as e: print('rerank skipped:', type(e).__name__)
else:
    assert len(rr) <= 5
    wide = k.env_context('atomic file write', limit=RERANK_FANOUT)
    assert {r['content'] for r in rr} <= {r['content'] for r in wide}, 'reranked hits must come from the fanout'
    print(rr.attrgot('metadata').attrgot('mod_name'))
```

## Docs index

Code chunks suit code, but a README or a `docs/` folder reads better as
whole sections. kosha keeps a third index for such prose, built on
litesearch’s `Index`, which splits documents by their headings and can
search, list and return whole sections. It lives in the shared data
directory (`docs.db`), next to the package index, and is created the
first time you use it.

`add_docs` adds a folder of documents, a single file, or a dict of
{title: text}, and returns the number of chunks added. `add_pkg_docs`
adds a package’s full README. `docs_context` searches the docs index. By
default it returns ranked sections, each with a `node_id` you can pass
to `k.docs.read` to get the whole section; `sections=False` returns the
raw chunks. The docs index uses the same embedding model as the code
indexes, so only one model is loaded.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Kosha.docs_context

``` python
    q:str, # the search query
    limit:int=5, # hits to return
    sections:bool=True, # ranked sections (with `read` handles) vs raw chunks
    **kw
)->fastcore.foundation.L: # forwarded to Index.sections / Index.search
```

*Search the docs index, returning whole sections by default or raw
chunks with `sections=False`.*

``` python
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

with TemporaryDirectory() as td:
    _dk = Kosha(dir=Path(td), xdg_dir=Path(td))
    n = _dk.add_docs({'install': '# Install\n\nRun `uv add kosha` to install kosha into your project.',
                    'search':  '# Search\n\nCall `env_context` to search installed packages by meaning.'})
    assert n > 0, 'docs index ingested nothing'
    assert len(_dk.docs) == n
    hits = _dk.docs_context('how do I install this', sections=False)
    assert hits, 'no docs hits'
    assert 'uv add kosha' in hits[0]['content']
    secs = _dk.docs_context('search installed packages')
    assert secs and _dk.docs.read(secs[0]['node_id'])['text']
    print(repr(_dk.docs))
```

## Keeping syncs fast

Indexing is meant to fit in an edit and search loop. Repo and package
updates touch only what changed. The call graph is optional, and
`sync(graph=False)` skips it when you need only search. The default
graph update reads changed Python files in one fast pass. The slower
full extraction runs only with `graph_mode='full'`. PageRank is
recomputed only when the number of edges has changed by more than 10%.
`graph_metrics=False` stops the recomputation.

``` python
_root = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'proj'; (_root/'.git').mkdir(parents=True)
(_root/'pyproject.toml').write_text('[project]\nname = "proj"\nversion = "0"\ndependencies = ["kkfake"]\n')
_sp = _root/'.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages'; (_sp/'kkfake').mkdir(parents=True)
(_sp/'kkfake'/'__init__.py').write_text('def hello(): return 1\n')
(_sp/'kkfake-1.0.dist-info').mkdir()
(_sp/'kkfake-1.0.dist-info'/'METADATA').write_text('Metadata-Version: 2.1\nName: kkfake\nVersion: 1.0\nAuthor-email: a@b.co\n')
_kp, _cwd = Kosha(dir=_root, xdg_dir=_root/'xdg'), os.getcwd()
os.chdir(_root)
try:
    test_eq(_kp.env_path, [str(_sp.resolve())])
    _kp.update_pkg('kkfake', embed=False, verbose=False)
    _md = L(_kp.env_st(where="package='kkfake'")).map(lambda r: jl(r['metadata']) if isinstance(r['metadata'], str) else r['metadata'])
finally: os.chdir(_cwd)
test_eq(set(_md.attrgot('version')), {'1.0'})
assert all(Path(m['path']).resolve().is_relative_to(_sp.resolve()) for m in _md)
_md.map(lambda m: (m['mod_name'], m['version']))
```
